metadata.text: 1. Chào mừng & Hướng dẫn học tập hiệu quả cùng AI Assistant Hello and welcome to English for Complete Beginners! In this lesson, you will learn how to greet people and introduce yourself with confidence. Common greetings include: 'Hello', 'Good morning', 'Good afternoon', and 'How are you?'. To introduce yourself, simply say: 'My name is...' or 'I am from...'. Let's practice pronouncing each phrase together step by step!

metadata.text: 2. Cài đặt tư duy phản xạ tiếng Anh (English Mindset) Hello everyone! Welcome back to our English Grammar lesson. Today, we are learning about Subject Pronouns and Object Pronouns in English. Look at the key example on the screen: I see them. In this sentence, 'I' is the Subject Pronoun, and 'them' is the Object Pronoun receiving the action. Subject pronouns always stand before the main verb: I, You, We, They, He, She, It. Object pronouns always stand after the verb or preposition: Me, You, Us, Them, Him, Her, It. For instance: They see me, She helps him, and We listen to them carefully. Always pay close attention to the position of the pronoun in your sentence to avoid mistakes. Now, let's practice speaking and making sentences with Subject and Object pronouns together!

metadata.text: 5. Phương pháp nghe thụ động (Passive Listening) & nghe chép chính tả Hello everyone! Today, we are exploring the Present Continuous Tense. We use the Present Continuous to talk about actions happening right now at the moment of speaking. The basic formula is: Subject + am / is / are + Verb-ing. For example: I am studying English right now, and she is reading a book. Look for signal words like 'now', 'at the moment', or 'currently' in your tests.

metadata.text: Bài học mới Welcome back! In this section, we will study Possessive Adjectives and Possessive Pronouns. Possessive adjectives describe ownership and are always followed by a noun: my book, your car. On the other hand, possessive pronouns replace both the adjective and noun: This book is mine. Let's review the pairs: my - mine, your - yours, our - ours, their - theirs, his - his, her - hers. Practice reading aloud these sentences to build natural English speaking reflexes!
